exposure: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection during pregnancy
outcome: Concurrent infections (Hepatitis B virus, syphilis, gonorrhea, chlamydia)
Antibiotic treatment for suspected neonatal sepsis
cohort: A large population of 22,604,938 live births in the United States from 2016-2021, with 107,761 complicated by maternal HCV.
finding: Maternal HCV infection during pregnancy is associated with certain sociodemographic factors (advanced maternal age, Medicaid insurance, smoking) and increased risks of concurrent infections and several adverse pregnancy and neonatal outcomes, including preterm birth, low birthweight, congenital anomalies, low Apgar scores, NICU admission, suspected neonatal sepsis, and ventilation.
